children: Russian is shifting its grains exports to the Baltic Sea following Ukrainian attacks on Black Sea infrastructure and shipping, Kpler analysts say. Russian grain exports out of the Black Sea have been minimal so far in October after escalating Black Sea disruption over the summer. But Russia is repurposing ports in the Baltic Sea to handle grains exports, the analysts say. For example, the port of Vysotsk, which typically handles coal, is exporting an increasing proportion of Russian grains. Baltic Sea exports can't offset the volumes lost in the Black Sea, however, they say. Wheat nudges 0.2% down at $6.27 a bushel, after peaking around $7.84 a bushel in August.
